description: Enables Optimizely users to manage translations centrally while working with any LSP or in-house team using supported tools.
releaseNotes:
# iLangL Localization Extension for Optimizely 12 — Release Notes

Package versions: `iLangl.Extension.Optimizely.V12` / `.Core` share one version;
`iLangl.Extension.Optimizely.V12.Commerce` has its own.

## 12.29.1.39 / Commerce 14.23.0.39 — 2026-10-30

### Fixed

- **Projects could be created without a website (domain).** Content whose
  website could not be determined — typically blocks or media stored in
  "For This Page" or "For This Site" asset folders — was ordered without a
  domain. Such a project did not appear under *Existing Project* when
  ordering a page from the same site, so authors could not add further pages
  to it. The connector now uses Optimizely's own site resolution
  (`ISiteDefinitionResolver`), follows asset folders to their owning page or
  block, and falls back to a start-page lookup if the resolver is unavailable.
  Content shared by all sites (global assets) is still ordered without a
  domain, by design.
- **Domain resolution failures are now logged.** Any item for which no website
  can be determined is written to the Optimizely log at *Information* level;
  lookup errors are logged at *Error* level instead of being swallowed.
- **Order dialog showed "READY TO DELIVER" for jobs already on the Delivery
  step.** The *Languages* step of the order dialog did not receive the
  `finalDelivery` flag that the Jobs view uses, so every completed job was
  labelled "READY TO DELIVER". The dialog now shows the same status and badge
  colour as the Jobs view.

### Notes for this release

- The status fix expects the Localization Hub `contentdetails` endpoint to
  return `finalDelivery` as the `jobs` endpoint already does. If the hub omits
  it, the dialog shows the hub step name instead of "READY TO DELIVER".
- Existing projects that were created without a domain are not changed by
  this release; set their domain on the hub side or recreate them.

## 12.29.1.38 / Commerce 14.23.0.38 — 2026-10-19

### Fixed

- **Jobs view returned HTTP 400 after selecting a custom status.** The
  *Status* filter mixes standard workflow states with custom hub state names.
  Selecting a custom name broke model binding of the request, and every
  subsequent filter change failed while that status stayed selected. The
  filter now sends statuses as strings, matching the hub API.
- **Delivery job failed when run by the scheduler without a user.** Saving
  translated content raises CMS Projects notifications, which require a named
  user. When the scheduled job ran anonymously (or the configured scheduler
  user did not exist in the site's user store) the save threw
  `ArgumentNullException`. The delivery job now always runs content saves under
  a named principal, falling back to `ilangl-scheduler`.
